response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior/staff engineer with strong developer-tooling instincts (test runners, assertion libraries, CI/CD, and prior work on the LabWindows/CVI IDE at National Instruments), but the core requirements of this role are not met. The role demands deep Java/Kotlin and JVM expertise plus solid Spring/enterprise-framework experience; the resume shows Java only as a secondary language in a 2016–2018 role, no Kotlin, no Spring/Quarkus/Hibernate, and no JVM build-tool or application-server work. Recent experience is concentrated in TypeScript/Node.js and DLang. The tooling interest and IDE background are genuine positives, but the JVM ecosystem gap is too large for a mid-senior IC expected to own enterprise-framework subsystems from day one.
strengths: Prior IDE development experience at National Instruments (LabWindows/CVI)
Strong developer-tooling track record: test runner, assertion library, MCP codegen
Long, senior-level career across complex systems and high-throughput services
concerns: No Spring, Quarkus, Hibernate, or application-server experience
No Kotlin; Java only peripheral and ~8 years stale
Recent work is TypeScript/Node and DLang, not JVM
